summary: Describes how to run WebSockets over a single stream of an HTTP/3 connection. The mechanism already existed for HTTP/2, and only the HTTP-version-specific details needed to be specified. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC explains how WebSocket connections can use a single stream in HTTP/3. It carries over the Extended CONNECT rules from HTTP/2 and specifies the HTTP/3 setting needed to enable them.

questions: how do websockets work over http/3
subtitle: HTTP/3 rules for using Extended CONNECT to bootstrap WebSocket streams.

tldr.problem: The WebSocket mechanism defined for HTTP/2 is also useful with HTTP/3, but its HTTP/3-specific details needed to be specified.
tldr.mechanism: The memo carries over Extended CONNECT semantics and registers the SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL setting for HTTP/3.
tldr.outcome: The HTTP/3 setting is registered with value 0x08, and stream closure represents closure of the WebSocket transport stream.

today: RFC 9220 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Adapting the HTTP/2 Mechanism
sections.content: RFC 8441 defines a way to run the WebSocket Protocol over a single stream of an HTTP/2 connection. RFC 9220 specifies how to use that mechanism with HTTP/3, where protocol settings must be registered separately.
sections.plainLanguage: HTTP/2 already had a way to carry WebSockets on one stream. This memo specifies the related details for HTTP/3.

sections.title: Extended CONNECT and HTTP/3 Settings
sections.content:
Extended CONNECT uses a :protocol pseudo-header field and defines semantics for the :path and :authority pseudo-header fields. The meaning of these fields and the setting is identical to HTTP/2. The HTTP/3 setting SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL has value 0x08, the same value used in HTTP/2.

If a server advertises Extended CONNECT but receives an unknown or unsupported :protocol value, it SHOULD respond with status 501 (Not Implemented). It MAY include more information in a problem-details response.
sections.plainLanguage: The client and server use Extended CONNECT to identify the WebSocket protocol on the stream. A server that does not support the requested protocol should return 501.

sections.title: Closing the HTTP/3 Stream
sections.content: HTTP/3 stream closure is analogous to TCP connection closure for WebSockets. An orderly closure is represented by a FIN bit on the stream. An RST exception is represented by an HTTP/3 stream error of type H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED.
sections.plainLanguage: The HTTP/3 stream has signals for normal and cancelled closure. These serve the corresponding roles of connection closure in the WebSocket protocol.

sections.title: Security and Registration
sections.content: The memo introduces no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 8441. IANA registers SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL in the HTTP/3 Settings registry with value 0x08, default 0 and permanent status.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC adds no security considerations beyond the earlier HTTP/2 specification. It records the setting and its default in the HTTP/3 registry.

references.text: McManus, P., "Bootstrapping WebSockets with HTTP/2", RFC 8441, September 2018.
Fette, I. and A. Melnikov, "The WebSocket Protocol", RFC 6455, December 2011.
